ssot: WRITER-AGENT-SSOT.md §9.0 item 4c, §9.3.1 rows H2 and H4
why: Item 4c asks for a non-publishing probe that narrows the note/ja 422 by bisecting the rejected body against note's draft surface. This file records the measurement that answers whether such a probe can reproduce the failure it is meant to diagnose. It cannot: the draft surface accepts the exact rejected bytes.
method: The incident draft n47735d9811e8 was read once, read-only, with the same authenticated GET publish-paid.py already performs. Its body was replayed against the draft surface on a throwaway scratch draft created for this measurement, whole and then as each half of the rejected paid split. No payload sent carried a status field and no publish endpoint was called. Requests were spaced 3 seconds apart.

incident.error_signature: NoteNativePublishError: Note native publish HTTP 422: {"error":{"code":"invalid","message":"本文に利用できない内容が含まれています。"}}
incident.recorded_payload_sha256_source: state/runs/daily-2026-08-07/gates/note-native-effect.json, written by publish-paid.py before the PUT

reconstruction.how: build_paid_publish_payload from scripts/note-publish/publish-paid.py was replayed offline against the draft body still held by note, sweeping every distinct separator block and a small set of tag candidates, and hashed exactly as publish-paid.py hashes it (json.dumps(payload, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True)).
reconstruction.significance: The exact bytes note rejected are reproducible offline from artifacts that still exist, with zero requests to note. Any later narrowing stage therefore starts from the real payload rather than a guess.

requests.label: readback after: draft_save whole incident body
cleanup delete scratch (retry with editor headers)
requests.note: the first DELETE returned 422 Unprocessable Entity solely because Origin/Referer/X-Requested-With were absent; note's delete requires the editor headers

verdict.measured: The exact rejected body, and each half of the rejected split sent on its own, were all accepted by POST /v1/text_notes/draft_save with HTTP 201 {"result":true}. No 422, and no other rejection, on any of the three.
verdict.structural: The rejected payload's fields are free_body, pay_body, separator, price and status:"published". draft_save accepts name, body, body_length, index, is_lead_form and hashtags. The paid split has no draft representation, which publish-paid.py had already measured independently on 2026-07-16 and recorded in its module docstring: paid type, price and paywall line are transient editor form state that note commits only on 投稿する.
verdict.consequence: A draft-surface bisection has no signal to bisect and cannot present note with the payload that failed. The item 4c probe cannot exist as specified. Building one would have measured a different validator on different inputs and returned a confident wrong answer.

not_verified: Whether the publish-surface 422 is deterministic. The PUT was never re-sent, because re-sending it is the one action that can create a public artifact. A single observed 422 is not proof of a stable rule.
Which element of the payload note objects to. This measurement narrows only by exclusion: note's draft validator finds nothing objectionable in these bytes.

Whether PUT /v1/text_notes/{id} with a non-published status would run the same validator. Not attempted: the risk that note publishes anyway cannot be bounded in advance, and a transient public artifact is still a public artifact.
